q: Every thermometer uses a physical property that varies with temperature, referred to as the _____ property.
e: Every thermometer uses a physical property that varies with temperature, referred to as the thermometric property. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: The thermometric property of a liquid-in-glass thermometer is the _____ of the liquid.
e: The thermometric property of a liquid-in-glass thermometer is the thermal expansion of the liquid. Most objects grow when they warm because the molecules move harder.

q: A liquid-in-glass thermometer consists of a thin glass bulb joined to a _____ tube with a narrow bore.
e: A liquid-in-glass thermometer consists of a thin glass bulb joined to a capillary tube with a narrow bore. The physics in this sentence is built around capillary.

q: When the bulb of a liquid-in-glass thermometer becomes warmer, the liquid in it expands more than the bulb so some of the liquid is forced into the _____.
e: When the bulb of a liquid-in-glass thermometer becomes warmer, the liquid in it expands more than the bulb so some of the liquid is forced into the capillary tube. The physics in this sentence is built around capillary tube.

q: The thinner the _____ wall is, the faster the response of the thermometer will be when the temperature changes.
e: The thinner the bulb wall is, the faster the response of the thermometer will be when the temperature changes. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred involving response.

q: The liquid used in a liquid-in-glass thermometer usually contains mercury or coloured _____.
e: The liquid used in a liquid-in-glass thermometer usually contains mercury or coloured alcohol. The physics in this sentence is built around alcohol.

q: Alcohol has a _____ freezing point than mercury so it is more suitable for low-temperature measurements.
e: Alcohol has a lower freezing point than mercury so it is more suitable for low-temperature measurements. You compare the unknown amount with a standard so the result is a number with a unit.

q: Thermocouple thermometers are electrical thermometers which make use of the _____ that develops when two different metals are in contact.
e: Thermocouple thermometers are electrical thermometers which make use of the voltage that develops when two different metals are in contact. The physics in this sentence is built around voltage. Current: the flow of electric charge.

q: Because of the small size of a thermocouple junction, thermocouple thermometers are used to measure _____ changing temperatures.
e: Because of the small size of a thermocouple junction, thermocouple thermometers are used to measure rapidly changing temperatures. The physics in this sentence is built around rapidly involving thermocouple.

q: Thermocouple thermometers can be used to measure much _____ temperatures than liquid-in-glass thermometers.
e: Thermocouple thermometers can be used to measure much higher temperatures than liquid-in-glass thermometers. The physics in this sentence is built around higher.

q: A resistance thermometer uses the fact that the electrical _____ of a metal wire increases with temperature.
e: A resistance thermometer uses the fact that the electrical resistance of a metal wire increases with temperature. Temperature tells you the hotness. Heat tells you energy transferred.

q: A resistance thermometer can measure temperatures accurately in the range _____ to 1200°C.
e: A resistance thermometer can measure temperatures accurately in the range -200°C to 1200°C. The physics in this sentence is built around -200°C.

q: A resistance thermometer is best for _____ temperatures, but it is bulky.
e: A resistance thermometer is best for steady temperatures, but it is bulky. The physics in this sentence is built around steady.
